name: Seated Guard Retention

phases.name: Establish Inside Position
phases.description: Keep knees between you and opponent. Fight for inside position on both sides.

phases.name: Frame on Contact
phases.description: When opponent closes distance, establish frames on biceps/shoulders to create space.

phases.name: Pummel for Inside Control
phases.description: Pummel arms and legs back to inside position whenever they are pushed outside.

phases.name: Manage Distance
phases.description: Use feet on hips or biceps frames to maintain distance; don't let them collapse your guard.

systemLogic.corePrinciple: Win inside position = keep guard. Lose inside position = get passed.

decisionTree.condition: Opponent bullies through with chest pressure
decisionTree.action: Shin frame or stand up — do not stay seated and let them collapse
Pivot on your butt, keep facing them, re-insert inside knee

exitStrategies: Stand up to technical stand-up position
Transition to supine guard if seated position is compromised
Enter shin-to-shin to create sweep opportunity

keyCorrections.issue: Both knees open to one side
keyCorrections.fix: Keep one knee pointing at each of their hips
Keep elbows in front of knees; arms are for framing, not posting
Stay on one hip, weight on one hand — dynamic base

moneyDetails.oneLiner: Inside position = guard. Lose it, get passed.
moneyDetails.mnemonic: Inside first, frame second, pummel always

safetyNotes: Avoid posting with straight arms — keep elbows bent. Protect your knees from lateral pressure.
fixItFast: Inside knees → frames on contact → pummel → reset distance
